methodology.instrumentation: Disposable WebGL and requestAnimationFrame wrappers, derived from the earlier scratch instrument-rendering.mjs hook; no production edits.
methodology.triangles: Actual TRIANGLES draw submissions, including actual render passes and instancing; not unique model topology.
methodology.resources: Created WebGL texture/buffer/program objects minus observed delete calls, across the instrumented page. Programs are not material counts.
methodology.timing: Synchronous drawing requestAnimationFrame callback wall time, including application work, driver waits, submission and hook overhead; neither isolated CPU nor GPU duration.
methodology.cpuTiming: Optional owned Chrome CDP Performance.enable({timeDomain:threadTicks}) and getMetrics bracket actual drawing callbacks, before asynchronous GPU-result polling. ThreadTime and TaskDuration cumulative seconds become CPU milliseconds per observed drawing callback, with explicit boundary-count uncertainty. All renderer-main-thread tasks, CDP/instrumentation overhead and unrelated page work remain included; this is not isolated rendering CPU.
methodology.fitting: Read public module fit counters before frames and refresh their DOM report afterwards by reselecting the same Idle animation, without changing appearance.
methodology.gpuTiming: Optional EXT elapsed-time queries span the owned Lab drawing callback. Results are polled in later animation frames without gl.finish or synchronous result waiting; unavailable/disjoint/busy/timeout samples remain explicit. GPU query duration is separate from callback wall time.
methodology.cancellations: Every request failure is retained with its observed phase; cleanup is labelled only during owned-context closure.

limitations: Desktop headless Chrome, not physical iPhone/iPad performance or heat acceptance.
Thirty drawing callbacks per profile are a bounded observation, not a general performance guarantee.

CDP threadTicks counters measure renderer-main-thread CPU across the aggregate window, not isolated rendering, process-wide CPU or worker threads. Boundary frame counts are observed around CDP reads rather than atomically at the metric timestamp.
GPU timer-query duration, when available, covers the submitted Lab callback commands rather than isolated shader or per-material work.
No geometry-fit acceptance is inferred from rendering counts.
